title: Sports Events
goal: Ask about event tickets and seating, make a viewing plan, and react while watching a game.

study.title: Choose seats and confirm the charge

runs.text: This fictional ticket card is already available for purchase:

rows.text: River City Tigers versus Harbor Hawks, Saturday at 4 p.m.
$25 each; C14 and C15 are available together.
$18 each; does not assign a particular seat in this offer.
Step-free entry at the West Gate; wheelchair viewing spaces in Section C; ask staff about space and companion-seat availability.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Are there two reserved seats together for Saturday?

turns.en: Are there two reserved seats together for Saturday?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Yes. C14 and C15 are available at twenty-five dollars each.

turns.en: Yes. C14 and C15 are available at twenty-five dollars each.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: What's the total, including the order fee?

turns.en: What's the total, including the order fee?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Okay. I'd like those two. Could you confirm the section and start time?

turns.en: Okay. I'd like those two. Could you confirm the section and start time?

turns.speaker: Employee

runs.text: Section C. The game starts at four.

turns.en: Section C. The game starts at four.

blocks.caption: Choose seats and confirm the charge · Customer & Employee

runs.text: gives entry without the same assigned-seat arrangement. Details vary, so ask
Does that ticket guarantee a seat?
makes the choice after the details have been explained;
I need a wheelchair viewing space and a seat for my companion. What's available?
Which entrance has a step-free route to Section C?
Describe the actual feature you need. An accessibility label alone may not answer it.
If the event is sold out, you can ask
or choose another event. No waitlist or discount is supplied in this card; those answers remain open.
In a separate fictional café, staff have confirmed that they will show the Tigers–Hawks game at 4 p.m. Tables are available from 3:30.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Are you showing the Tigers game on Saturday?

turns.en: Are you showing the Tigers game on Saturday?

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Could we get a table at three thirty? There are three of us.

turns.en: Could we get a table at three thirty? There are three of us.

turns.speaker: Staff

runs.text: Yes, we can reserve one for three thirty.

turns.en: Yes, we can reserve one for three thirty.

turns.speaker: Customer

runs.text: Great. So three people at three thirty, and the game starts at four.

turns.en: Great. So three people at three thirty, and the game starts at four.

blocks.caption: Arrange to watch elsewhere · Customer & Staff

runs.text: means display the broadcast here, rather than stage the contest in the café.
supports or enjoys a team, player or activity;
reacts to a near success or a tense moment.
can express a fan's identification with the team, even when the fan did not play.
After a lost lead in an invented game:

turns.speaker: Fan B

runs.text: Yeah. We were two points ahead, and now we're behind.

turns.en: Yeah. We were two points ahead, and now we're behind.

turns.speaker: Fan A

runs.text: There's still time. Come on, Tigers!

turns.en: There's still time. Come on, Tigers!

blocks.caption: React to what happens · Fan A & Fan B

runs.text: is a swear word expressing frustration here; listeners differ in how they receive it.
gives another voice for the same feeling. Use a choice that fits your intended effect and company. Swearing is not required to sound involved.
I don't think that was a foul
preserves uncertainty. You can disagree about a moment without inventing knowledge of a rule or insisting that everyone share your team loyalty.
Use the ticket card. Ask for two seats together, check the total fee, then choose the seats or decline. Staff answer using C14 and C15.
Ask about a wheelchair viewing space and companion seating. Staff say
. Ask which entrance to use; that answer is supplied in the card. Keep the space request unconfirmed.
Use the café scene to arrange a table for three at 3:30. Confirm the table time and game time separately.
Then change your role: you do not follow either team. Give an honest response.

Your team was ahead and has fallen behind. React with the frustrated or less forceful option, then add encouragement. A friend disagrees about a foul you did not see clearly; respond without claiming certainty.

“Are those two seats together? Is the total fifty-two dollars? I'll take them.” / “Could you check the space and companion seat? Which entrance is step-free?” / “Three people at three thirty, and the game at four—that's right?” / “I'm rooting for the Tigers” or “I'm just watching.” / “That's frustrating. There's still time—let's go!” / “Maybe. I didn't see it clearly.”
speak both sides using the supplied facts, then cover the examples. Change your purchase decision or team preference later.
Did the price, seating need and plan become clear? Did you distinguish availability from confirmation, and your reaction from a fact you could actually establish?
